interface.signature: def solve(T: int, test_cases: list[tuple[int, list[int], list[tuple[int, int]]]]) -> list[int]: ...

preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is between 1 and 30 inclusive.
For each test case, the number of vertices N is between 1 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(markers) == N for (N, markers, _) in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the number of markers equals the number of vertices N.

preconditions.expression: all(all(marker in {0, 1, 2} for marker in markers) for (_, markers, _) in test_cases)
preconditions.description: Each marker in the bag has an integer value of 0, 1, or 2.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == N - 1 for (N, _, edges) in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the number of edges is exactly N - 1 (forming a tree).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= N and 1 <= v <= N for (_, _, edges) in test_cases for (u, v) in edges)
preconditions.description: For each test case, all edge vertices u and v are between 1 and N inclusive.

postconditions.description: The result contains exactly one integer per test case.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(unattractiveness, int) for unattractiveness in result)
postconditions.description: Each result is an integer representing the minimum unattractiveness.
The unattractiveness is a non-negative integer.

postconditions.expression: all(any(all(abs(assignment[u] - assignment[v]) <= unattractiveness for (u, v) in edges) for assignment in permutations(markers) if len(set(assignment)) == N) for (N, markers, edges) in test_cases for unattractiveness in result)
postconditions.description: For each test case, the computed unattractiveness is the minimum possible maximum absolute difference between connected vertices in any valid assignment of markers to vertices.
